questions.stem: When a polythene rod is rubbed with a cloth, the rod becomes negatively charged. What has happened during this process?

options.text: Neutrons have been removed from the rod
Protons have moved from the rod to the cloth
Positive charges have been created on the cloth
Electrons have transferred from the cloth to the rod

questions.explanation: When charging by friction, only electrons move between materials. The polythene rod gains electrons from the cloth, giving it a net negative charge.

questions.stem: What happens when two negatively charged objects are brought close together?

options.text: They repel each other
They attract each other
Nothing happens
One becomes positively charged

questions.explanation: Like charges repel each other. Two negatively charged objects both carry the same type of charge, so they push apart.

questions.stem: A charged balloon sticks to a neutral wall. Which process causes this attraction?

options.text: Electrostatic induction
Radiation
Conduction
Convection

questions.explanation: Electrostatic induction causes charge separation in the wall. The near surface of the wall acquires the opposite charge to the balloon, resulting in a net attractive force.

questions.stem: Why are fuel tankers fitted with earthing straps?

options.text: To reduce air resistance during transport
To prevent the fuel from freezing
To allow static charge to flow safely to the ground and prevent sparks
To increase the speed of fuel delivery

questions.explanation: Friction from flowing fuel can cause charge to build up on the tanker. Earthing straps provide a conducting path to the ground, allowing charge to flow away safely and preventing dangerous sparks that could ignite fuel vapour.

questions.stem: In an electrostatic precipitator, how are smoke particles removed from the air?

options.text: Smoke particles are heated until they evaporate
Smoke particles are filtered through a fine mesh
Smoke particles are dissolved in water sprays
Smoke particles are charged and then attracted to oppositely charged collecting plates

questions.explanation: In an electrostatic precipitator, smoke passes through a charged metal grid which charges the particles. The charged particles are then attracted to oppositely charged collecting plates, removing them from the air.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes how lightning occurs?

options.text: The Sun heats the ground, causing positive charges to rise into the atmosphere
Ice crystals rubbing together in clouds cause charge to build up, and when the voltage is high enough, the air becomes conducting and a massive current flows
Protons in clouds transfer directly to the ground through raindrops
Wind causes electrons to be stripped from air molecules at high altitude

questions.explanation: Lightning occurs when ice crystals in clouds rub together, building up charge (typically negative at the cloud base). This induces positive charge on the ground, and when the voltage is high enough, air becomes conducting and a massive discharge occurs.

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of using electrostatic spray painting compared to conventional spray painting?

options.text: Less paint is wasted and the coating is more even, including hard-to-reach areas
The paint dries faster
The paint colour is brighter
The paint becomes waterproof

questions.explanation: In electrostatic spray painting, charged paint droplets are attracted to the earthed object, coating all surfaces evenly including hard-to-reach areas. This results in less waste and a more uniform finish.
